newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rules out public sector wage rise in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rules out public sector wage rise in Jan.

text.p: Brazilian Administration Minister Luiz Carlos Bresser Pereira has ruled out a public sector wage rise in January, although the possiblity of some increase later in the year existed, the minister's spokesman said.
Spokesman Roberto Piza said Bresser had not discarded the possibility of wage increases later in the year but that this would depend on the performance of government revenue and expenditure.
"The minister doesn't rule out the possibility of an increase later in the year but we are not talking yet in terms of what percentages this might involve," Piza told Reuters.
Brazil's civil servants have not received pay increases for two years with the government trying to slash its operational deficit from 1995's 5.0 percent of gross domestic product.
The operational deficit for 1996 is expected to have been some 4.0 percent of GDP.
The Jornal do Brasil newspaper reported Thursday that the budget for 1997 allowed for an average 7.5 percent salary increase in the public sector.
The budget must still pass through Congress.
